issues.description: resolve(from, '..', s) changes semantics of resolvedSources and may break absolute source paths
issues.detail: The change from `resolve(s || '', from)` to `resolve(from, '..', s || '')` alters the base used when resolving relative sources. The `pathe`/Node `resolve` is right-to-left: previously each source `s` was resolved (with `from` only used if `s` was relative), but now `from` is treated as a directory base and `'..'` walks up one level — which is correct for treating `from` as a *file path* (so its directory is the base). However, if `s` is an absolute URL (e.g. `file:///...`, `webpack://...`) or an absolute path, the old code returned `s` unchanged; the new code still returns `s` (resolve ignores earlier args when later one is absolute) but the protocol/URL handling diverges across platforms. Worth a unit test for: absolute path source, URL-form source (`webpack://`), empty source, and Windows path separators.

issues.description: Synchronous fs reads inside getSourceMap callback can hurt performance on large stack traces
issues.detail: `getSourceMap` is invoked during stack parsing for every external frame. It calls `existsSync` and `readFileSync` per frame and additionally `convertSourceMap.fromMapFileSource` may trigger another `readFileSync` for the .map file. With deep stacks across many distinct external files this becomes O(N) sync I/O on the reporter path, with no caching. A per-file memoization (Map<filePath, SourceMap|undefined>) would avoid re-reading the same module's source map repeatedly within one error report.

issues.description: Default import of convert-source-map may fail under strict ESM interop
issues.detail: `import convertSourceMap from 'convert-source-map'` relies on synthetic default interop. convert-source-map@2 is published as CJS with named exports (`fromSource`, `fromMapFileSource`). Depending on `tsconfig.esModuleInterop` and the runtime ESM loader, `convertSourceMap.fromSource` could be undefined at runtime. The `@types/convert-source-map` types declare the namespace shape, so TS will compile, but Node ESM consumers of vitest's dist could see a TypeError. Prefer `import * as convertSourceMap from 'convert-source-map'` or named imports for safety, and add a smoke test that actually exercises this path under Node ESM.

issues.description: Returning '{}' as a fallback for missing map files may produce a malformed JSON sourcemap and throw downstream
issues.detail: `createConvertSourceMapReadMap` returns the literal string `'{}'` when the target path does not exist. `convert-source-map.fromMapFileSource` will then parse this as `{}` which lacks required fields (`version`, `sources`, `mappings`) and downstream `@jridgewell/trace-mapping` will likely throw or yield garbage. Either return `undefined`/throw a controlled error that fromMapFileSource handles, or short-circuit and return undefined from `extractSourcemapFromFile` when the map file isn't found.

issues.description: No caching of file read or map extraction — same external file may be parsed multiple times per run
issues.detail: External module files (e.g. node_modules deps with inline source maps) often appear in many test failures. Each call re-reads and re-parses the file. Consider a WeakRef-keyed or LRU cache on filePath -> SourceMap|undefined, ideally invalidated by file mtime. Even a simple per-TestRun Map would substantially reduce redundant disk I/O when many errors share the same offender (transpiled dep).

issues.description: Silent swallowing of errors during sourcemap extraction
issues.detail: `extractSourcemapFromFile` has no try/catch. A malformed inline sourcemap comment, a corrupt .map sibling, or a permissions error on `readFileSync` will throw out of `getSourceMap` and likely abort stack parsing — producing a worse user experience than the previous behavior (no source map applied). Wrap the body in try/catch and return undefined on failure, optionally logging via `project.ctx.logger.warn` in debug mode.

issues.description: Mixing 'pathe' and 'node:path' in the same file is inconsistent
issues.detail: The file already imports `resolve` from `pathe` (for cross-platform POSIX-style joining) but the new code imports `path` from `node:path` and uses `path.resolve` / `path.dirname`. On Windows this could produce backslash-separated paths that diverge from how the rest of the file produces source map URLs. Prefer `dirname` and `resolve` from `pathe` for consistency.

issues.description: Comment claims module exists 'due to Vitest fetch module' — a regression risk if that invariant changes
issues.detail: The condition `!mod?.transformResult && existsSync(file)` is gated on an internal invariant of Vitest's module graph. If a future refactor changes how external modules appear in `vite.moduleGraph`, this filter silently disables itself. A small comment with a link to a test that pins the invariant, plus a guarded fallback (try sourcemap extraction even when transformResult exists if the file is clearly outside the project), would be more robust.

issues.description: Snapshot now points to .ts source — verify CI fixture provides the .ts file on disk
issues.detail: The updated snapshot expects `transpiled.ts:22:8` for a file installed under `node_modules/@test/test-dep-error`. This implies the test fixture package ships the original .ts alongside the compiled .js (or the inline sourcemap embeds the source content). If a future test-fixture change drops the .ts on disk, the resolved frame will resolve to a path that doesn't exist on the developer's machine and the snapshot will diverge. Confirm the fixture ships .ts and add a test ensuring both inline (sourcesContent) and external (.map sibling) paths work.

issues.description: @types/convert-source-map placed in dependencies rather than devDependencies
issues.detail: `@types/convert-source-map` is added under `dependencies` of `packages/vitest/package.json`. Type packages are normally devDependencies; shipping them as runtime dependencies bloats install size for vitest consumers and is inconsistent with the convention used for other `@types/*` packages (which are listed in dependencies here too, so this may be intentional for bundling — worth a quick sanity check that the publish flow strips or bundles these).

dissents.topic: Whether to add caching for source map extraction

positions.position: Per-file sync reads on every error frame is wasteful; add an LRU/Map cache keyed by filepath.

Errors are exceptional and the cost is bounded by stack depth and unique external files. Premature optimization without a measured regression — ship as-is and add caching if profiling shows it matters.

dissents.topic: Whether '{}' fallback for missing map files is acceptable

positions.position: Returning a string '{}' that parses to an invalid SourceMap object is incorrect — downstream tools assume a well-formed map and may throw. Return undefined and let the caller skip.
convert-source-map's API expects a string; '{}' is the documented escape hatch that yields 'no useful map' rather than crashing the comment parser. The behavior is intentional and copied from Vite.

The old `resolve(s, from)` was actively wrong for relative sources — pathe.resolve is right-to-left so `from` was being treated as a directory layered on top of `s`, which inverts intent. The new ordering with explicit `..` correctly says 'directory of `from`, then apply `s`'.
Better still to use `resolve(dirname(from), s)` — it expresses intent directly and avoids the `..` trick which is brittle if `from` is ever a directory rather than a file.

review.summary: The PR correctly fixes a long-standing bug: external modules whose stack traces pointed at compiled JS now resolve back to their original source via the file's inline or sibling source map. The core change in `packages/utils/src/source-map.ts` (resolving sources against `dirname(from)` instead of treating `from` as the input) is a legitimate fix, though the `resolve(from, '..', s)` formulation would read more clearly as `resolve(dirname(from), s)`. The new `getSourceMap` hook in `test-run.ts` is reasonable but adds unbounded synchronous I/O per stack frame with no caching, no error handling, returns a malformed '{}' fallback that could crash downstream sourcemap parsers, mixes `pathe` and `node:path`, and uses a default import of a CJS module that may fail under strict ESM. None of these are merge-blocking — there are no P0 issues — but the error-handling and caching gaps should be addressed before merge, and the default import should be verified against vitest's published ESM build.
